why: With the cue standing in for the saturated mode part, theta0.25 on the 328 adds about a quarter of the linear long-horizon part (41 items from base cue 164 to RL 205) plus a small leftover of the mode part, giving about 181.
At a = 0.5 the mode part is saturated and about half of the linear long-horizon part is present, so the cued 328 gets about 164 + 0.5*41 ≈ 185-188.
Code-RL carries the shared mode part but none of the math-specific long-horizon part that the 328 rewards, so it sits near theta0.5 (about 187), well below RL's 205-206.

Code-RL lacks the long-horizon component that makes RL's long solutions long, so on the 328 it writes about 0.7-0.75 times RL's 9,316 tokens per problem, the same ratio as on MATH-500 (3,337 vs 4,694).
theta0.5 cue at about 187 against RL plain at 206 on the 328 is about -19/328 ≈ -5.8 points, because half of the long-horizon part is missing.
Code-RL cue at about 187 against RL plain at 206 is about -5.8 points, because the math-specific long-horizon component is absent.
Both carry the saturated mode part and roughly equal long-horizon credit on the 328 (Code none plus extra plain-flip, theta0.5 half), so the theory puts them level.
Any RL-Zero delta carries the domain-general mode part, and MATH-500 barely rewards the long-horizon part, so a cued Mix model lands with the theta0.5 / Code-RL group near 450.
A General RL-Zero delta still carries the shared mode part, so with the cue it should reach the 440-450 band where theta0.25 and Code-RL sit, above base cue 410.
Code-RL 3.0 carries the shared mode part and, like 3.1 Code with the cue (450), loses little on MATH-500 for lacking the long-horizon part.
An IF RL-Zero delta carries the domain-general deliberate-then-commit part, so with the cue it should land in the 440-450 band, not at base cue 410.
